task_name: The conversation's paperwork under the state root

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each has production lines behind it. (a) 'the phase prompt ... written where a restart can find them': `prepare` builds `<root>/coordinating-session/<id>/phase-prompt.md` through `#promptPath` and writes `prompt.text` at it, returning that path. (b) 'the record of the conversation ... written where a restart can find them': the same method writes `<root>/coordinating-session/conversation.json` with `#recordFor`, serialised as two-space JSON plus a trailing newline. (c) 'the record is read back as a CoordinatingConversation': `recall` reads the record path and `#conversationFrom` rebuilds a real `CoordinatingConversation` out of `ConversationId`, `RepositoryName` and `CheckoutRoot`, which is what `open-coordinating-session.ts` already consumes through the `ConversationRecords` port. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The **TDD:** line names two tests and fixes their assertions. `it('answers the path of the prompt it wrote for that conversation')` is in the diff with the write double recording path and text (`const write = vi.fn(async () => {})`) and asserts exactly the two things the plan wrote down: the literal path returned (`expect(path).toBe(PROMPT_PATH)` with `PROMPT_PATH = '/state/coordinating-session/2b1a6c2e-.../phase-prompt.md'`) and the text written at it (`expect(write).toHaveBeenCalledWith(PROMPT_PATH, PROMPT_TEXT)`). `it('raises conversation-not-recorded instead of reading a malformed record as no conversation')` feeds `'{not json'` through the read double and asserts `rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ConversationNotRecorded)` — the same input, the same expected value, and it is the assertion that separates the malformed record from `null`, which is what the sentence fixes.

Walked name by name against the `Contract (backend/src/infrastructure/disk-conversation-records.ts)` block. `export class DiskConversationRecords extends ConversationRecords` ✔ (the port in `domain/ports/conversation-records.ts`, with `super()` called). `static readonly DIRECTORY = 'coordinating-session'`, `RECORD = 'conversation.json'`, `PROMPT = 'phase-prompt.md'` — the three literal values ✔. Constructor destructures `{ read, write, root }` with `read: (path: string) => Promise<string | null>`, `write: (path: string, text: string) => Promise<void>`, `root: string` ✔ (aliased as `ReadText`/`WriteText`, same signatures). Prompt at `<root>/coordinating-session/<conversation id>/phase-prompt.md` ✔, record at `<root>/coordinating-session/conversation.json` ✔, record body `{conversation, repo, root}` with the id, `owner/name` and the absolute path ✔, `prepare` answers the prompt's absolute path ✔. `recall` answers `null` when the record is absent (`if (text === null) return null`) ✔, a `CoordinatingConversation` when it reads ✔, and raises `ConversationNotRecorded` when the file is there and unreadable as that shape ✔ — including a well-formed JSON object with wrong fields, because the value objects validate `unknown` and their throw is caught. A failed write raises `ConversationNotRecorded` too ✔.

Row by row over the rows this diff bears on. D-10 ('Everything new under backend/ is TypeScript'): both files are `.ts` with erasable syntax only, and `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` is green. D-25 ('the backend hands over paths and pastes none of that text into a prompt'): `prepare` returns the prompt's path and the text only ever reaches the file — the adapter never composes or relays prompt text anywhere else. D-16 ('cmux leaves the backend'): the module names no cmux and the test requires nothing installed. D-13 ('No phase is stored'): the record holds conversation id, repository and root — evidence, not a phase. D-1, D-11, D-18, D-21, D-22, D-26 and the entrance button's literal are rows this diff leaves alone, which complies. No row is implemented with a different value.

Exemplars: the diff plays the role of `backend/src/infrastructure/disk-implementation-start-registry.ts` (a record under the state root) and matches its idiom — injected `ReadText`/`WriteText`, `static readonly DIRECTORY`, a private `#isRecord` guard, a `recordFor` projection and `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` plus a trailing newline. The sibling adapter test `claude-conversations.test.ts` is matched in shape (real value objects, doubles built per test, names that are sentences). RULES — `conventions/architecture.md`: infrastructure adapter implementing a domain port, importing only domain; `src/infrastructure/` is where `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` puts adapters and `**Files:**` pins the path, so the flat layout is the repository's declared choice, not this diff's. `conventions/style.md`: no comment, no docstring, every identifier English, and every function hangs off the type (statics `#isRecord`, `#recordFor`, `#conversationFrom`; methods `#recordPath`, `#promptPath`, `prepare`, `recall`) — no module-level function. `conventions/boundaries.md`: what comes off disk is validated on entry with no cast (`new ConversationId(parsed.conversation)` on an `unknown`), and the validation error does not leave the boundary — it is translated into `ConversationNotRecorded` quoting the other side's own words. `conventions/simplicity.md`: every symbol has a caller — the three statics are the contract's, `#isRecord` is reachable (a JSON scalar reaches it). `conventions/decisions.md`: the record's shape is decided once, in `#recordFor`, and the test asserts the literal payload rather than re-deriving it. `conventions/domain.md`: the type names are the domain's, not the filesystem's. DEFECTS.MD, rule by rule — (1) closed vocabulary: nothing here classifies; the `none|live|unresumable` vocabulary is the endpoint's, a later task's, and no string is compared by hand and no dispatch has a catch-all. (2) raw map as the return value of logic: `#recordFor` returns a `JsonRecord`, but it is private, its only consumer is the `JSON.stringify` one line below it in the same class, and the parsed map in `#conversationFrom` is projected straight into value objects — that is the serialization boundary in one step, not logic reading a map by key. (3) two fields that have to agree: the record's three fields are independent facts, and the absence of a record is `null` in the type rather than an empty string or a zero — no sentinel. (4) an error named for where it happens: `ConversationNotRecorded` names what happened and inherits `ConversationFailure`, not the root. TWO CLASHES, DECLARED AND LEFT OUT OF THE FINDINGS because the implementer could not have written any other diff: `conventions/testing.md` asks that 'Both failure causes of every adapter are told apart in its tests ... the test proves one is not an instance of the other', and `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` asks that every family under `PlanFailure` name its two causes; the task's Contract block fixes one class for both ('raises ConversationNotRecorded when the file is there and cannot be read as that shape ... A write that fails raises ConversationNotRecorded too'), and `exceptions.ts` is not in `**Files:**`, so a second leaf could not be added here. The defect is the plan's. Secondly, `conventions/boundaries.md`'s 'An unknown key is a rejection' is read against its own next clause ('Project only the keys you consume'): the record is written by this very adapter, not a foreign system, and the exemplar reads it the same way. Noted and not a finding: the value-object constants of this test file (`josemerca/ct-loop-sandbox`, the `2b1a6c2e-…` id) repeat those of `claude-conversations.test.ts`'s `Governed` type with a different root and no mother between them — the backend has no mother infrastructure at all today, so this is the repo's standing idiom rather than something this diff introduced.

Does not apply: both files in the diff are `new file mode 100644` and the diff carries no `-` line at all, so there is no pre-existing assertion, case or test that could have been removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by `backend/src/infrastructure/disk-conversation-records.ts`, which is production code: `#promptPath`/`#recordPath` compute the paths with `node:path`'s `join`, `prepare` performs both writes and returns the path, `#recordFor` builds the record and `#conversationFrom` rebuilds the domain object. The test's scaffolding is only the two `vi.fn` doubles standing in for the filesystem — the cut right before the external system — and no expected value is hard-coded into production. Revert the adapter and every one of the six tests falls.

The diff writes only the two files `**Files:**` declares, both `(create)`, and every line inside them serves a sentence of the task: the three statics, the constructor and `prepare`/`recall` are the Contract block; the six tests are exactly the six names under `**Tests:**`, no more and no fewer. No refactor, no rename, no adjacent fix, nothing touching `plugin/skills/brainstorming/`, `POST /start-plan`, the gates or `Home` — the four things `### Out of scope` names. There is no hunk of the plan file in this diff, so no amendment to rule on.

Six new tests, measured on the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no randomness, no sleep and no path outside the doubles — `read` and `write` are `vi.fn` closures and the only paths are the literals `/state/...`, never touching a real filesystem. Isolated: every test builds its own `read`, `write` and `DiskConversationRecords`; the module-level constants are frozen value objects nothing mutates, and no test depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the adapter did — the path it returned, the literal pair `(path, text)` and `(path, json)` the write port received, the `CoordinatingConversation` `recall` rebuilt (`expect(recalled).toEqual(CONVERSATION)` together with `expect(read).toHaveBeenCalledWith(RECORD_PATH)`), and the two failures raised — which is `conventions/testing.md`'s 'the literal request sent' for an adapter, not a stub's return value. Each of the six would fall if the adapter's lines were reverted. Beyond the three I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md`: none of its five anti-patterns fits — the doubles are the external system itself, the mock setup is three lines against a five-line body, and no test-only method was added to the production class.
